text: The Radon-Nikodym derivative d(mu)/d(nu) exists (for sigma-finite measures) precisely when:
choices: mu and nu are mutually singular
mu is absolutely continuous with respect to nu
explanation: Absolute continuity mu << nu (nu(A) = 0 implies mu(A) = 0) is exactly the hypothesis giving a density d(mu)/d(nu). Mutual singularity is the opposite situation, and equality/finiteness are neither necessary nor sufficient.
